intl_finance.document: Rutgers International Student Financial Statement (ISFS) plus a bank letter or statement from the sponsor's financial institution on bank letterhead, uploaded to the Rutgers Global portal together with a passport photo page; needed to receive the I-20

deadlines.label: ISFS and bank documents for the I-20 (after you accept the offer of admission)
deadlines.note: No calendar date published. Documents must be signed and dated no more than six months before Rutgers receives the completed I-20 application.

intl_finance.notes: The balance shown must be greater than or equal to the amount on the ISFS. The 2027-2028 sample ISFS (source 3) lists estimated annual costs of $66,759 for year 1 (tuition and fees $40,839; room and board $17,805; miscellaneous $8,115), asks for bank statements for a checking or savings account, expects years 2-4 to rise 5 percent a year, and adds $5,000 for a spouse and $4,000 per child. Rutgers says to keep the original bank letter for the visa interview.

notes: Source 1 says Rutgers requires one short original essay (Common App 250-650 words; 3,800 characters on the Rutgers Application) and that there are no supplemental essays required for the Common App. It also says a short statement is required if you choose to be considered for honors. The Honors College essay prompt and limit could not be read from its official page (honorscollege.rutgers.edu/admissions/how-apply returned HTTP 403), so no honors prompt is listed; search summaries describe an up-to-500-word question but this is unconfirmed. The first-year and international pages do not name the application year; the ISFS sample is for 2027-2028.
